title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level network configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents (4 intent families), model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, execution contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and at most one repair call per intent. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Execution accounting: completed episodes = 300; model calls used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We report all preregistered design choices, analysis details, and execution accounting to inform future NetOps preregistrations and replication.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces aim to let network operators express desired changes in free text rather than low-level device commands, promising reduced operator effort and faster change workflows. However, single-pass LLM outputs frequently contain syntactic omissions, ordering errors, or semantic violations that can break invariants required for availability or safety when applied to real networks [1], motivating gated generate→verify→repair pipelines that put deterministic oracles between language-generation and execution. Prior work shows that verifier-aware training or multiple iterative repairs can improve correctness in infrastructure-as-code contexts, but reported gains depend strongly on baseline model competence, sampling semantics, and repair budget [2],[3].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we asked: does constrained prompting (structured templates + explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics?

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a reproducible synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Exact execution and analysis results showing baseline success = 149/150 and guarded success = 150/150, yielding a marginal +0.67 pp improvement that is not statistically significant under the preregistered test (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological lesson: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects, and generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) must be explicitly stated because they change the estimand and operational interpretation.
sections.related_work:
Three related strands inform this study. First, intent-to-configuration translation and intent-driven NetOps work document the persistent challenge of producing verifier-sound artifacts from free text and report modest semantic-correctness on public benchmarks, motivating post-generation checks and formal verification integration [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures—including verifier-guided fine-tuning and policy-informed resampling—have yielded correctness gains for IaC and configuration-repair tasks, but reported improvements vary with baseline competence and repair budgets [3],[4]. Third, security analyses of tool-augmented LLM agents show claim-to-action risks where unchecked textual claims can become harmful actions; these motivate auditable gating and verifier-aware planning in NetOps pipelines [5].

How this study differs. Many prior studies measure average-case gains when repairs or retraining are unrestricted; by contrast our preregistered trial isolates the marginal effect of a single allowed repair applied to the identical initial candidate under shared_initial_candidate semantics. This operationally realistic but conservative estimand clarifies the marginal value of lightweight runtime guards versus more invasive model improvements [3],[6].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and frozen prior to any model interactions (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Confirmatory design: paired_binary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; planned N=150 confirmatory intents; per-intent protocol: one initial shared generation and at most one guarded repair call. The preregistration specified inclusion/exclusion rules (deterministic ambiguity detector and verifier-coverage checks), a missingness policy (one deterministic retry on API timeout then mark failed), and a power plan targeting an absolute +15 pp improvement at ≈80% power under conservative discordant assumptions.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by the preregistered generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and span four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). Pre-execution mapping unit-tests and verifier-coverage checks were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred (exclusions = 0). Representative tasks (six archived examples) include medium–very_hard difficulty labels and nontrivial required sequences, showing the generator produced structured, policy-constrained intents.

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair budget and session isolation. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail plus normalized final-configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and diagnostics. These artifacts were archived and used as the primary outcome oracle.

Runtime-sampling semantics and shared_initial_candidate meaning. Per reviewer request and per preregistration reporting requirements: the archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). No numeric temperature or fixed random seed was enforced; therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. The execution contract used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. Because the initial candidate is identical across conditions, the baseline success rate reports the validity of that single sampled candidate; the guarded vs baseline contrast thus isolates the marginal effect of at most one repair applied to that same candidate (and not differences that would arise from independent resampling per condition).

Execution accounting, contamination controls, and retries. Planned episodes = 300 (150 paired tasks × 2 conditions). Completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. The adapter recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 1. Contamination checks reported zero flags and pre-execution mapping unit-tests passed. Missingness policy was not invoked because no provider-call failures or parsing failures occurred.

Scoring and statistical analysis. Primary outcome: deterministic validator pass/fail (binary). Confirmatory test: exact two-sided McNemar on the paired contingency counts. Complementary uncertainty quantification: 95% bootstrap percentile confidence intervals computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor and code are archived and were applied without post-hoc changes; all numeric facts below are drawn directly from archived analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Execution summary and audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Model_calls_used = 151; artifact_hash_count = 1058. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}. Contamination flags = 0 and exclusions = 0.

Primary numeric outcomes. Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Paired_contingency_table.csv and condition_summary.csv are archived and match these reported counts and rates.

Repair diagnostics and iteration counts. Only a single guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate: median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). The single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator; archived validator traces record validation_before and validation_after normalized_configurations, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_codes for each episode. Representative task examples (e.g., task-000001: shutdown->mtu->vlan->restore) show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count and valid=true for both conditions in most episodes.

Representative artifacts and diagnostic breadth. Representative tasks (000001–000006) illustrate a range of difficulty labels (medium, hard, hard, very_hard, very_hard, very_hard) and required sequences (atomic paired MTU changes, make-before-break uplink switchover, safe access transfer). Despite this nontrivial set, the tested model produced near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus. These representative artifacts substantiate that the generator produced constrained policy-driven intents rather than trivial single-command prompts.

Sensitivity checks and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats missing guarded outputs as failures was not needed because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No parse failures occurred and contamination unit-tests passed. The observed results therefore derive from a complete paired sample without missingness-driven bias.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and impact on power. The preregistration's power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline success rate (target detectable effect = +15 pp). Observing baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 removed most headroom for the guarded pipeline to demonstrate a large absolute gain, producing a classical ceiling effect that invalidated the original power assumptions. Practically, this shows that short baseline-calibration pilots that estimate model competence on the chosen task bank are essential before fixing N in preregistered NetOps trials.

Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because the execution contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics, the baseline measures the success of the single initial sampled candidate while the guarded condition measures the marginal value of at most one repair applied to that same candidate. An independent-sampling design (resampling per condition) would estimate a different quantity (average per-condition performance over independent draws) and could produce larger observable differences if sampling variance is nontrivial. Thus the present result bounds the marginal benefit of a one-repair guard in a low-variance sampling regime for gpt-5-mini on the frozen corpus.

Operational and audit-value considerations. Even when marginal verifier-pass improvements are small, guarded pipelines yield operational benefits not captured by a binary metric: auditable normalized configurations, deterministic diagnostics (violation_codes, parsed_command_count) that accelerate human triage, and explicit repair prompts that standardize operator review. These nonstatistical operational affordances can justify guarded architectures in practice.

Limitations and external validity. The study used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic deterministically generated corpus restricted to small topologies (4–32 nodes), and a one-repair budget. Therefore results do not generalize to other model families, larger heterogeneous networks, or designs that permit multiple repairs or independent per-condition resampling. The deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; while mapping unit-tests were run and archived, residual construct-validity risks remain. Security aspects (adversarial prompt-injection) were intentionally out of scope for this confirmatory trial and require separate targeted experiments.

Design implications for future NetOps preregistrations. We recommend that preregistrations explicitly specify generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling), include concise baseline-calibration pilots to estimate baseline competence and calibrate N, preregister repair-budget sensitivity analyses, archive mapping/verifier unit-tests prior to batch runs, and report provider-call audits (model_calls_used, stage_counts) to document execution budgets and stage-level behavior. These procedural elements materially affect estimands and interpretability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single deterministic-verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically small and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly state generation semantics because these choices determine the estimand, statistical power, and operational interpretation. Evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, broader model families, and production-scale topologies remains important future work and requires separate preregistration and power planning.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
